clue.text: Old PM has packed in cycling

indicators.note: cycling rotates a word, moving its front letter round to the back
something packed in is stuffed inside another word, and these words also mean gave up

parts.note: the word has with its first letter rotated to the end
to pack in a job is to quit it

explanation.surface: A former prime minister has given up cycling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Packed in' does double duty: it means QUIT and also signals that QUIT is packed inside the rotated word.
explanation.definitionFit: H. H. Asquith was the Liberal British prime minister from 1908 to 1916.

clue.text: Help player wanting debut

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, and a debut is a first appearance, so the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: a bassist is a bass player in a band

explanation.surface: A musician who wants a first gig asks for help.
explanation.walkthrough: BASSIST loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To assist is to give aid, a direct synonym of help as a verb.

clue.text: Medley of quite bold tunes?

indicators.note: a medley is a mixture, so the letters that follow are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Asks for a mixture of rather daring melodies.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer and also supplies the mixed letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A quodlibet is a musical piece combining several popular melodies in a humorous way.

clue.text: He's wasting time introducing Liberal to topless equestrian

indicators.note: topless means without the top, which in a down clue is the first letter
introducing something to a word puts it inside

parts.note: an equestrian is a rider; the top is cut off
L is the abbreviation for Liberal

explanation.surface: A man introduces a politician to a half-naked horse rider instead of working.
explanation.walkthrough: L goes into RIDER minus its R.
explanation.definitionFit: An idler is a lazy person, someone who passes the hours doing nothing useful.

clue.text: Supporter's condition almost has Bobcat installing college without foundation

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is cut
a foundation is the base, which in a down clue is the final letter

parts.note: has, almost

indicators.note: installing means putting something inside, so one piece goes into another

parts.note: Bobcat is the setter, who refers to themselves as me
Merton is an Oxford college; its last letter goes

explanation.surface: The setter putting up a crumbling college building sounds like a supporter's ailment.
explanation.walkthrough: The supporter is a foot, which holds you up. Setters often call themselves 'me', and Merton is a college of Oxford University.
explanation.definitionFit: Hammer toe is a deformity where a toe bends permanently downward, a medical condition of the foot.

clue.text: Literary folk giving up time for final character castings

indicators.note: giving up one thing for another means swapping it out, so one letter is exchanged

parts.note: the Brontë sisters, the novelist family
T is the abbreviation for time
Z is the last letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Writers trade in deadlines for the last letter, as if retiring from the craft.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the T in BRONTES for Z.
explanation.definitionFit: Bronzes are sculptures cast in bronze metal, so castings is a fair plural noun for them.

clue.text: Pipe music from the south pervades empty bar

indicators.note: pervades means spreads through, so one piece goes inside another
empty means the inside is cleared out, leaving the outer letters

parts.note: the outer letters of bar

indicators.note: in a down clue, reading from the south means reading upwards

parts.note: an air is a tune

explanation.surface: Southern-style music drifts through a deserted pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From the south' only works in a down clue, where reading upwards starts at the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: A briar is a tobacco pipe made from the root of the briar heath plant.

clue.text: Teach Dora about figures

indicators.note: about suggests turning round and moving letters into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Instructions to tutor a girl named Dora in maths.
explanation.definitionFit: Octahedra are solid geometric shapes with eight faces, so they are figures.

clue.text: Like a region of Australia — aiming high and all ignoring the odds?

indicators.note: aiming high in a down clue means reading upwards

parts.note: Oz is a nickname for Australia

indicators.note: ignoring the odd positions leaves only the even letters

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: Describes an ambitious Australian region that defies the odds.
explanation.definitionFit: Zonal describes something relating to a zone, which is a region.

clue.text: New York Times supports society spreading road stone

indicators.note: spreading out suggests the letters are scattered and rearranged

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for society
the four letters of road rearranged
the standard abbreviation
x is the multiplication sign

explanation.surface: A newspaper backs a society that is laying a road made of stone.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'supports' means the newspaper's letters sit below the rest, holding them up.
explanation.definitionFit: Sardonyx is a gemstone, a type of onyx with layers of sard.

clue.text: Plunder ship, releasing its cargo and fuel

indicators.note: a ship that unloads its cargo is emptied, leaving only its outside letters

parts.note: the outer letters of ship
oil is a fuel

explanation.surface: Pirates loot a vessel after it has unloaded its goods and fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoil, usually as spoils, is goods taken as loot or booty, the noun sense of plunder.

clue.text: Guide taking in source of Nile after me gets wetter

parts.note: moi is French for me, often used jokingly in English

indicators.note: taking in means absorbing something, so one piece goes inside the other
the source of a river is where it begins, so only the opening letter is wanted

parts.note: to steer is to guide
the first letter of Nile

explanation.surface: A tour guide who visits the Nile's source after me ends up wetter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After me' means the French word for me comes first, with the guide following it.
explanation.definitionFit: A moistener is something that makes things wet, so the noun means a wetter.

clue.text: Length of time Royal Marines managed without playing nim

indicators.note: playing about suggests the removed letters can come out in any order
managed here is read as handled or worked over, so the letters are rearranged
without means lacking, so some letters are removed from the phrase

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written; nim is a game of removing counters

explanation.surface: The Royal Marines got by without a game of nim to pass the time.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove M, I and N, scattered through Royal Marines, then rearrange the remaining nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A solar year is the period of the Earth's orbit round the Sun, a standard period measuring duration.

clue.text: I'm surprised in brothel lounge

indicators.note: in tells you the word sits inside the following words of the clue

parts.note: found spanning the two words

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in shock at finding themselves in a brothel's lounge.
explanation.definitionFit: Hello can be an exclamation of surprise, as in 'Hello, what's this?'

clue.text: How one might carelessly blend dynamite with sulphur?

definitions.text: How one might carelessly blend dynamite with sulphur?

indicators.note: doing something carelessly throws things into disorder, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
S is the chemical symbol for sulphur

explanation.surface: Who would mix explosives with sulphur so casually?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the wordplay: only a distracted person would mix explosives like that.
explanation.definitionFit: Absent-mindedly means without paying attention, which is the only way anyone would make such a dangerous mixture.

clue.text: Cycle needing Raleigh's capital for development

indicators.note: needing here means lacking, so a letter is missing

parts.note: a revolution is one full cycle

indicators.note: 'capital' keeps only the first letter of 'Raleigh'

parts.note: the first letter of Raleigh

explanation.surface: A Raleigh bicycle needs capital investment for its development.
explanation.walkthrough: Raleigh is a British bicycle maker, which feeds the cycling surface. Remove R from REVOLUTION.
explanation.definitionFit: Evolution is gradual change and growth, the same as development.

clue.text: Frequency of drink being served short in hostelry by church

indicators.note: served short means a drink comes with less than it should, so a letter is cut off
in places one piece inside another

parts.note: an inn is a hostelry
cider loses its last letter
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Complaining about how often drinks come up short at the pub near the church.
explanation.definitionFit: Incidence is the rate at which something occurs, which is its frequency.

clue.text: Occasion for spinsters to be certified as bachelors?

definitions.text: Occasion for spinsters to be certified as bachelors?

parts.words: spinsters to be certified as bachelors
parts.note: surface reading: unmarried women declared unmarried men

parts.words: Occasion for spinsters to be certified as bachelors?
parts.note: setter's reading: bachelors are graduates, so this is the ceremony where women receive a bachelor's degree

explanation.surface: Asks when single women are officially turned into single men.
explanation.walkthrough: Bachelor means both an unmarried man and a holder of a first university degree.
explanation.definitionFit: The day when students receive their university degrees at a graduation ceremony.

clue.text: Doctor prematurely restraining one in a cheerless way

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor

indicators.note: restraining means holding something in, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: too early means prematurely
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A doctor restrains a patient too soon and does so gloomily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a verb, but it gives the usual abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Drearily means dully or gloomily, an adverb matching the phrase.

clue.text: What determines the value of imported bread in a ready market?

definitions.text: What determines the value of imported bread in a ready market?

parts.note: surface reading: loaves brought in from abroad, sold in a market

parts.words: What determines the value of imported bread in a ready market?
parts.note: setter's reading: bread is slang for money, so imported bread is foreign currency, valued against your own

explanation.surface: Asks what sets the price of foreign loaves at a market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bread' is slang for money, and a 'ready market' hints at ready cash.
explanation.definitionFit: The rate at which one currency converts into another fixes what foreign money is worth.

clue.text: Depth charges ward off Bill

indicators.note: to charge is to load or fill, so one piece is put inside

parts.note: to avert is to ward off
D is the abbreviation for depth

explanation.surface: Depth charges are used to fend off a man named Bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depth charges' reads as anti-submarine bombs, but D is loaded into AVERT. Bill is a poster, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill is a printed notice or poster, a form of advertisement.

clue.text: I'm going to stop working with gold outside

indicators.note: outside means one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
a machine that dies stops working

explanation.surface: Someone retiring with a gold watch announces their departure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'm going' is the definition, not part of a sentence about someone leaving work.
explanation.definitionFit: Adieu is a French farewell, said when one is leaving, hence 'I'm going'.

clue.text: Meetings without prospects in Bury

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the following word is taken away

parts.note: interviews are formal meetings
a prospect is a view

explanation.surface: Job meetings with no prospects in Bury, a Lancashire town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bury' looks like the town near Manchester, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To inter is to place a body in a grave, a formal word for bury.

clue.text: Cover garden areas before lady strips

parts.note: flower beds are garden areas
pre- means before

indicators.note: to strip something is to take its covering off, so the outer letters go

parts.note: lady with its outer letters removed

explanation.surface: A woman undresses in front of the flower beds, which are covered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strips' looks like a noun or a striptease verb, but it tells you to peel the outside off the word lady.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedspread is the decorative top cover laid over a bed.

clue.text: He composed possibly the best part of Things to Come

definitions.text: He composed possibly the best part of Things to Come

indicators.note: composed means put together, so the letters are arranged afresh
the best part of a word is most of it, here the middle once the ends are trimmed

parts.note: the middle five letters, without the ends

explanation.surface: Names the composer of the score for the film Things to Come.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Arthur Bliss wrote the music for the 1936 film Things to Come; bliss is also the joy of the world to come, so the clue works as a straight reading too.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Bliss was the English composer whose score for Things to Come became famous.

clue.text: The fear of God

parts.note: surface reading: the idiom for terror or religious awe
setter's reading: the word comes from the Greek god Pan, whose sudden shouts terrified people

explanation.surface: The familiar phrase for being terrified.
explanation.walkthrough: The word derives from Pan, the Greek god of the wild, believed to cause sudden groundless fear.
explanation.definitionFit: Panic is sudden overwhelming fear, and etymologically it is the fear sent by the god Pan.

clue.text: This power of perception cannot be acquired thus

definitions.text: This power of perception cannot be acquired thus

parts.note: surface reading: a gift of insight that cannot be learned
setter's reading: split the answer in two and it describes being taught, the very route this faculty cannot take

explanation.surface: Says that a certain insight cannot be gained through lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: Split into two words, the answer reads 'in tuition', meaning by teaching, the very way this faculty cannot be obtained.
explanation.definitionFit: Intuition is instinctive understanding without conscious reasoning, so it is not taught.

clue.text: Jog in the altogether around the centre of Bingley

indicators.note: around means wrapping one piece outside another

parts.note: in the altogether is an idiom for naked

indicators.note: the centre picks out the middle letter of a word with an odd count

parts.note: the fourth of seven letters in Bingley

explanation.surface: Someone runs naked around the middle of Bingley, a town in West Yorkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jog' reads as running, but it means a gentle push. G sits inside NUDE.
explanation.definitionFit: To jog someone is to give them a slight push, which is what a nudge is.

clue.text: Privates cover ground for year, new territorials having been discharged

indicators.note: ground means crushed or milled, so these letters are broken up and reformed

parts.note: taken as written
Y is the abbreviation for year
N is the abbreviation for new

indicators.note: discharged means emptied of its load, so only the outer letters stay

parts.note: the first and last letters of territorials

explanation.surface: Soldiers take cover on the ground, a year after new reservists were discharged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Privates' looks like soldiers and the Territorials are Britain's army reserve; here privates are private parts. Y-fronts are men's briefs with an upside-down Y seam.
explanation.definitionFit: Y-fronts are men's underpants, a garment that covers the genitals.

clue.text: Cipher note penetrating rear of college chapel

indicators.note: penetrating means pushing into, so one piece goes inside the rest
the rear of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the last letter of college
N is the abbreviation for note
a crypt is an underground chapel or vault

explanation.surface: A coded message slips into the back of a college chapel.
explanation.walkthrough: N goes between E and CRYPT.
explanation.definitionFit: To cipher a message is to put it into code, which is to encrypt it.
